utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. The Chamber understands that it would be useful to fill in a few moments awaiting for a document, and fortunately that Mr. Tarculovski's counsel, Mr. Apostolski, is ready to step into the break and serenade us for ten minutes. Is that right, Mr. Apostolski?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely, Your Honours. Good morning. I have tried last night to see whether I could make my presentation shorter. In relation, very briefly, Your Honours, with your leave, I would like to respond to the response of the Prosecutor to the provisional release brief for the accused Tarculovski because of humane reasons, and I would like to respond to their mainly erroneous information contained in the Prosecution's response. Towards this end, I would like to ask the usher to help me distribute court binders. The general conclusion is that the Defence of Johan Tarculovski was confused when it received the Prosecution's response. The Defence believes that the Prosecutor has made a mistake and responded to a brief for provisional release of the accused Boskoski. As an argument against the provisional release of the accused, the Prosecution uses the alleged and unconfirmed support and the influence of the accused Boskoski in Macedonia; and as a combination of it, it shows a photograph of a billboard with a photograph of Boskoski, and I will speak about it later. The Prosecution does not provide any evidence in support of their allegations, other than the statement of the investigator, Thomas Kuehnel, who is the source of many uncorroborated and erroneous information. First, the Prosecutor erroneously alleges that the guarantee of the Government of the Republic of Macedonia does not indicate how will the government fill its promises that the accused will be prevented from influencing witnesses and victims or influence in any other way the administration of justice. The guarantee indicates precisely that the accused will be under 24 hours' surveillance, which will prevent him from any way of exerting influence or making contacts. Secondly, the Prosecutor alleges that the accused still has influence over his active supporters. It has never been proven that the accused has ever had active supporters. Secondly [as interpreted], it is not proven that he has now any active or passive supporters. The accused was just an ordinary inspector for security of persons, and he has never had subordinates. Furthermore, the Prosecutor indicates that the return to power of VMRO-DPMNE Party, to which the accused belongs, brings in doubt the implementation of the guarantee. The Defence wishes to clarify that the party, VMRO-DPMNE, has been divided into two parties since 2001. One of the parties retained the name VMRO-DPMNE, while the second is VMRO-NARODNA or VMRO People's Party. Completely, the leadership of VMRO-DPMNE of 2001 is now part of VMRO-NARODNA Party. You can see this in tab 1, and there is the report of the Peace and War Reporting Institute of 2nd of June, 2005. In the elections in 2003, President of VMRO-DPMNE became Nikola Gruevski, a very young liberal reformator [sic] who was very well known in the public as a successful Finance Minister. Nikola Gruevski and the former leader of VMRO-DPMNE, Ljupco Georgievski, started an open conflict which lasts to this very day. The overall executive committee was changed in 2003, and it was those people who won the elections in 2006, with pro-European and economic agenda. You can see this in tab 2 of the court binder, and that is a report of Radio Free Europe of 9th July 2004. The governments consists now of VMRO DPMNE, the Democratic Party of the Albanians, and the new Social Democrats. VMRO NARODNA has had only seven MPs elected and is now in a position. You can see it is in tab 3 of the court binder. This is an excerpt of World Book of Facts on Macedonia from 2007, and you can also see there's a list of Ministers in the present government. With regards to the cooperation of the Republic of Macedonia with the Tribunal, the Prosecutor claims that many Macedonian officials still feel an open, hostile sentiment towards the Tribunal and openly question the supremacy of the Tribunal over the Macedonian law and procedure. This conclusion of the Prosecutor is arbitrary and without any evidence in its corroboration. The Prosecutor does not indicate any official from Macedonia who is openly hostile towards the Tribunal. It is the opposite. The Macedonian Prime Minister, Nikola Gruevski has visited the Tribunal on the 14th of September 2006. You can see this in tab 4 of the court binder, and it was not just him. It was also the vice-president of the Government of the Republic of Macedonia, together with the Minister of Justice and the Minister of the Interior, who have also visited the Court, and they extended active support and cooperation to the ICTY. As a result of all this, recently 20 Macedonian judges and prosecutors came for a training in international criminal law here to the Tribunal. The Defence, in the response to the allegations of the Prosecutor in the relation of the candidate status of Macedonia in EU and NATO, confirms that the expected accession of Macedonia to NATO in 2001 and the start of negotiations for accession into the EU in 2008 makes Macedonia a serious partner in the international relations, a partner who has assumed serious obligations. We attach as annexes a statement from the meeting of the President Bush with the Prime, Minister Nikola Gruevski, as well as the meeting with Italy's Prime Minister, Romano Prode in relation of the accession of Macedonia to NATO and to the EU. You can see this in tab 5 of the binder, where there is also the photograph from the meeting of the -- of [indiscernible] with the Prime Minister. At the same time, the election of Mr. Srgjan Kerim as the President of the General Assembly of the United Nations, Srgjan Kerim is an Ambassador of the Republic of Macedonia and is an ethnic Turk, shows that the minorities in the Republic of Macedonia have free access and progress in all professions. Furthermore, the Prosecution claims that some requests for assistance have been left unanswered and some have been answered only partially by the Government of the Republic of Macedonia. We, hereby, submit evidence received from the Prosecution regarding any request for assistance requested from Macedonia, and that is contained in tab 6, where we conceded the Prosecutor has submitted 122 huge requests to Macedonia, while left unanswered are just four. More than 1.200 documents have been received, and many of them bear the label "State Secret." At the same time, just 40 per cent of the Defence's requests for assistance have been answered, which gives rise to the notion that the Prosecution has been treated with priority. With regards to the influence over the witnesses and victims, we believe that the assumptions of the Prosecution, that the ethnic Macedonian witnesses are afraid because of the repercussions of their testimony against them and their families and that they will be treated as traitors of Macedonia is completely erroneous, arbitrary, and unsupported, with any single evidence item. The Prosecution has not identified any pressure or any risk, or has not learned that some of the witnesses haven't signed the summons because of this reason. Furthermore, the Prosecution claims that since the Macedonian public follows the trial with great intensity, and since there is a climate of tension, it results in Prosecution witnesses asking for protection measures immediately before their testimony. First, the Macedonian public is not following the trial intensely. There is not a single accredited journalist to follow the trial. There is no live feed, just from time to time there are very modest reports in some medium. Secondly, the Prosecutor, without any evidence, claims that there is a climate of tensions, and such climate does not exist. The fact that the witnesses ask for protection measures immediately before giving their testimony might be due to the fact that they are not -- insufficiently informed about the Prosecution about the procedure or they were or not led well by the Prosecution. The Prosecution claims several times in their response that the accused, Tarculovksi, enjoys the support of the police. This is just an arbitrary phrase which the Prosecutor's office uses without any evidence for it or any proof of it. The Prosecutor's office did not identify a single supporter of Tarculovski, and the Defence strongly resents such abstract assessments. The Prosecution claims that some insider witnesses are with withdrawn or they could not remember some facts related to the accused. It is again that the Prosecution failed to identify a single witness who could not remember anything related to Tarculovski. If the Prosecution is having problems and does not have the case according to their wishes, it does not mean that Johan is to blame for this. They should look for the reasons within the Prosecutor's office. At the same time, why didn't the Prosecutor's office mention the so-called crime-based witnesses who give two or three different statements about a single event, and they could not remember facts from their previous statements? Was it Johan who has exerted influence over them in order for them to change their testimony? The Prosecutor claims that some witnesses have been threatened over the phone. Again, the Prosecution failed to provide evidence that Mr. Johan Tarculovski has any connection with this. Your Honours, we must also speak about the personal assessment of Mr. Thomas Kuehnel, the investigator, that Johan Tarculovski must not be released provisionally because he now plays the role of the Trial Chamber in this. The Defence believes that his role is to collect facts and verify them. We believe that his statement shouldn't be taken into consideration because his information are uncorroborated and they are hearsay information. In relation to the reasons for the provisional release and whether they are classified as humanitarian, the Defence claims that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The Prosecutor claims.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- that the reasons from the cases Hadzihasanovic and Kubura and Prlic could not be compared to the reasons in the Tarculovski case, because in both those cases provisional release is sought because of illness or deaths in the families. But the Defence maintains the position that if humanity respect the death, it should also celebrate and respect life. If the provisional release is to allowed to assist ill members of the family, it should be used to assist one's wife who is alone taking care of two children without the assistance from the husband. Thank you for the time you allocated for me, Your Honours, and I think that this response will give you a more complete idea about our request for provisional release of Mr. Johan Tarculovski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Apostolski. People are eager to speak in every direction. Mr. Mettraux, seeing my head is turned that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I think I should start so that Mr. Saxon may address our submission as well, Your Honour. We'll be very, very brief. We don't have any submissions to make in relation to the merit of the application. This is very much a matter between the Tarculovski Defence and the Trial Chamber. I would like, however, to make very brief submissions in relation to a comment which has been made by my colleague, Mr. Apostolski, when he pointed out that the response of the Prosecution appeared to be a response to an application by the Boskoski Defence rather than the Tarculovski Defence, and I can say that we fully agree with what our colleague has just said. Your Honour will have found a picture of our client in one of the annexes, which is a picture which appears in a billboard, the Prosecution says, in Skopje with a message saying: "Truth for Macedonia." And in its response, the Prosecution makes submissions which we would like to read to the Chamber. It's at paragraph 21 of the Prosecution response. It says: "Billboards depicting Boskoski have been placed in public locations with a message of support, 'Truth for Macedonia.'" The Prosecution goes on to say this: "The Macedonian population understand this action as a single of encouragement towards the two co-accused." There's no reference to any evidence, to anything, to any document, Your Honour. In any case, even if that were the case, we don't see anything wrong with anyone showing support for our client, nor do we see anything wrong for anyone asking for the truth for Macedonia or anyone else. The Prosecution goes on to make those submissions: "This message is also perceived as a sign of opposition towards the current ICTY proceedings." Again, Your Honour, no evidence, nothing to support that claim. "This type of propaganda," the Prosecution says, "has raised the already tense climate amongst the Macedonian population and has brought more pressure and fear to the witnesses and victims." Again, this is a baseless assertion without any evidence to support it. Your Honour has made it very clear that the Trial Chamber does not wish to get in a tug-of-war between counsel and that we should keep to the matters which are relevant to these proceedings, and we fully agree with Your Honour in respect to that position. However, the Statute guarantees that our client will benefit from, among other things, a presumption of innocence, and that presumption is binding on the Prosecution as well. We've indicated that in a number of filings the Prosecution has made what we consider to be collateral attacks on our client without any reasons and without any basis for it, and we ask that the Trial Chamber be warned not to repeat those attacks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mettraux. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just briefly, Your Honour, I'd like to respond to a couple of points that my colleague Mr. Apostolski made. In this binder of materials that has been provided to the Chamber and the parties, we see at tab 6 a spreadsheet, and indeed it's correct what my colleague said. This was a spreadsheet prepared by the Prosecution and provided to the Defence. It was prepared by the Prosecution in response to a request by our colleagues from the Defence for disclosure of materials related to requests for assistance to the Government of Macedonia and responses to those requests for assistance, and the Prosecution produced this spreadsheet in order to give some clarity to the matter and to show the information that had been requested and then the information that had been received and disclosed to the Defence. However, Your Honour, what this spreadsheet does not indicate, because the Prosecution was not asked to indicate it, it does not indicate whether responses to requests for assistance were fully complied with. And, quite frankly, there were many requests for assistance over the years where the response has been, shall I say, quite minimal. My colleague Mr. Apostolski referred to a meeting here in the ICTY with Prime Minister Gruevski in September of last year and several other members of the current Macedonian government. At that meeting, the Prosecutor, Carla Del Ponte, provided a new request for assistance to Mr. Gruevski, pointing out a list of earlier requests for assistance, for which the response had been, at best, partial, and providing copies of those earlier requests for assistance. And that letter was provided in September, and to date the Prosecution has heard nothing more. That's all, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon. The Chamber, assisted by those further submissions, will give detailed consideration to the motion. Now, are we ready to proceed? We better have the witness in. Is there something else, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: A very minor point, Your Honour, but perhaps it's best before the witness comes in. I'd simply ask that perhaps the Chamber could ask our court reporters to check something that I noted last night that is on page 2772 of the transcript. At line 12 and 13, there is a reference to the name "Goran," and then the last name given there is "Stojkov," and I may have been dreaming at the time, Your Honour, while I was on my feet, but my strong recollection is that the surname provided by the witness at the time was a very different surname. And there is another reference at line 16. Again we see the first name "Goran" and the last name "Stojkov," and it's my recollection that the surname given was a very different surname and, quite frankly, much more difficult to pronounce and to write. I'm just asking perhaps if the tapes could be checked. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps to assist, Your Honour, we have the same recollection as the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. The request will be conveyed to the reporters to check the tapes, and you will all be aware how difficult it is to precisely catch names not only of places but, in particular, of people when they are merely spoken in the course of our proceedings. Could we have Mr. Hutsch, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, may the Prosecution inform the Chamber of one short fact?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Relevant facts are always of interest, Mr. Saxon. What is this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I hope this will be considered relevant. It relates to the witness Vehbi Bajrami. You'll recall, I believe it was last week, where the Prosecution recommended that an addendum that had been admitted into evidence as part of the 92 bis statement or package with the witness Vehbi Bajrami be actually withdrawn, because the Prosecution suggested that that particular addendum had been admitted due to a miscommunication, and there was actually no legal basis for the admission. The Trial Chamber agreed with the Prosecution's submissions, but asked the parties to check to make sure that it would not be necessary for the witness to return, and the Prosecution has reviewed the transcript. The Prosecution has spoken with our colleagues from the Defence, and it's our understanding that both parties are in agreement that there is no need to bring this witness back, and that's what I wanted to convey to Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon. If the matter was left unresolved, in view of what has been said, the Chamber will order the withdrawal of that document from the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Hutsch.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Once again, the affirmation still applies, and Mr. Saxon, I'm sure, is getting nearer to the end of his examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, before we leave the events of 12 August 2001, I'd like to go back for a moment to what you observed inside the village of Ljuboten on that day. Did you observe any members of the Macedonian Army?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you observe any members of the National Liberation Army inside the village?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to ask our Court Officer's assistance, please, if Prosecution Exhibit P314 can be brought up on e-court, please. I think we're looking at the wrong image. The image we're looking for is -- that's it. I'm wondering whether the image on the left, which contains the map and the plastic overlay, if we could simply focus on that image, please, instead of a split screen. There you go. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, just very briefly, to refresh our memories, you see, in the middle of that map, in the area around the village of Ljuboten, we see two small blue circles. Do you see those blue circles?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, yesterday, you indicated that those blue circles indicated places where mortar fire impacted. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, the upper blue circle has the time "0607" next to it; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then there is a circle beneath that and we see the time 10:18. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters, once again, would like to ask for all parties to mind that our language is much more concise and we need time to interpret.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, our colleagues in the interpreting booth have just admonished us that we need to speak more slowly and pause between question and answer. All right? So on this map, after 10.18, you did not note or record any mortar impacts in Ljuboten; is that what this indicates?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could move now to Prosecution Exhibit P308, please, and these are, Mr. Hutsch, your notes from 12 August 2001. They're at tab 11 of the binder that you should have. I want to review something with you, please. If we can move to the next page of these notes, we see on this page, at 0748 hours, there's information from a telephone call with Mr. Beqiri. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. There's no information here about mortar fire or houses on fire in the village; correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn to the next page, please. And, again, on this page, there's no references to mortar fire or homes on fire in the village; is that fair?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn to the next page, please, which is after the -- now, that top line: "No fire from Ljuboten at 0827 hours," again, in this instance, the word "fire," you're referring to gunfire; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Down below, we see, after the spearheads entering Ljuboten, you refer to some explosions, a detonation flash; and then down below, at 8.34, it says: "Roof house at entry to town on fire." Right?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page, please. And we see on this page there's no information related to mortar fire landing in the village or homes on fire; is that fair?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's one information above, just with the symbol for a mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see. And that symbol for a mortar, does that mean an impact or a firing of a shell?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: An impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Can we -- but, again, there's no recording here of more homes on fire; right?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page, please. Now, on this page, at 1100 hours, we see references to explosions, RPG, machine-gun, AK-47, and then the line below that: "Fire, northern part of Ljuboten," and the word "slowly." Can we move to the next page, please. And then we see that entry ends: "... moving south." So the fire was slowly moving south, and, again, the reference to "fire" was in reference to gunpowder; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Gunfire, yes. Below that, we see the words: "Nine houses burning." So you noted that at around 11.00; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Then below that, we see "1150 hours" and some information; and below that, we see "1215 hours," and then we see: "14 houses burning. Rifle fire waning." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So about two hours after you had recorded last impacts of shells in the village of Ljuboten, because the recording you made on Exhibit 314 was made at 10.18. Just under two hours later you recorded: "14 houses burning"; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page, please. And here on this next page, at 1300 hours, we see: "Fire weaker." And, again, is that reference to gunfire?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But then below that, we see a line: "Approximately, 20 houses burning." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. So if my mathematics is correct - and I'm the first to admit often it's not - about two hours and 45 minutes after you recorded the last impact of mortar shells in the village of Ljuboten, you noted that there were about 20 houses in the village that were burning or on fire; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could turn now, please, to what is tab 23 in your binder. Mr. Hutsch, after the 12th of August, did you return to the village?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you remember the date that you returned to the village?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I returned on the 14th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you go into the village itself?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you have a notebook with you?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can you look at what's on the screen now. The first page, N003-0016, can you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is this notebook from the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Your notebook?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And there's a green rectangle at the bottom with some words in German in it. Is that the newspaper that you were working for at the time?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you entered the village on the 14th, were you accompanied by an interpreter or interpreters?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I was accompanied by two interpreters; an Albanian-speaking one and a Macedonian-speaking one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Today, are you willing to provide the Chamber with the names of those interpreters?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to just explore with you briefly some of the notes that you wrote here. First of all, we see it looks like a "T" with some letters under it. There's a "T" with the number "1" on one side and the number "2" on the other side. Can you tell us, please, what you were recording here?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was doing a sketch about the situation out of my memories when I found two dead bodies that we were talking about yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see. So you were making -- on the 14th, you were making a sketch of the bodies that you saw on the 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did this sketch on the evening of the 12th out of my memories.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see. Okay. But you wrote it into the book that's marked "14 August"?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Below that, we see: "Ljuboten, 0945 hours," and then the words: "Elmaz Jusufi." Did you have a conversation with this gentleman, Mr. Jusufi?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see some information here, it says: "Son Rami, 33, shot by members of the Ministry of the Interior members on Sunday, car destroyed. MUP uniformed, but not masked, entered the property around 0820 hours." Below that: "Around 20 of them were in the front yard. Rami reportedly tried to lock the front door, which was open." Then if we go to the next page, please, we see your notes in German on the right; and up at the top of the first page we see, towards the top: "Door was reportedly blasted open. Rami was riddled hail of bullets. Rami was hit in side and stomach." And below that, it says: "MUP then reportedly poured petrol on the car and set fire to it." Is this the information that Mr. Jusufi provided to you on that day?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Below that, we see the word or the name "Aziz Bajrami, (66)." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then some notes below: "Hid together with eight women of the family." Below that: "Ordered to leave the house. Men with hands to the back of their heads, kneel. Men separated from women. Hand over passports. 'Don't look up or you're dead.'"? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Below that, it says that: "3.000 Deutsche marks belonging to Aziz Bajrami were taken by a policeman," and towards the bottom of the page, it says: "The group was all herded together. All kneel. Sulejman kicked in the head several times, reportedly began to bleed from the nose." Do you see that information?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And is this information -- is this information that you received from Aziz Bajrami on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn to the next page, please. The top of the next page, we see a line: "Together with Muharem Bajrami (65)," then below that: "after that, Muharem was reportedly shot." Below that, we see a line: "MUP members reportedly shouted, 'The pig is still moving.' "Fresh shots," and then below that, a quote, "Long live Arkan." Below that, we see: "All lay down again. Sulejman was kicked again several times. He got up blearily and tried to run away." And then below that: "Then the Chetnik who kicked him shot him, then all started shooting." Then below that, a question mark and the words: "Aziz was shot in the hand." Is this the information that Aziz Bajrami gave you on the 14th of August?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, I would seek to tender these notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: On what basis?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: On the basis that these notes are a nearly contemporous [sic] of the events that occurred in Ljuboten on the 12th and that they also corroborate the evidence of a number of witnesses who have testified in this proceeding already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The evidence of this witness might corroborate, but not the notes. They are merely an assistance, but let me hear Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Simply to make the same point that we've made in the last two days. We're going to ask questions to this witness in relation to the reliability and the truth of the notes in this document, so at this stage we won't formally object, but we will certainly take it on with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The notes will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P320, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you turn now to tab 25, please, which is 65 ter number 168. Mr. Hutsch, if you can take a look at this document, the first page has the ERN number R037-6821; and, first of all, if we can step back for a minute, in September 2001 -- or let me step back even further. Did there come a time in 2001 when you stopped working as a journalist in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it came.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And about when was that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in the middle of September, when I was called up as a reserve officer to go to the staff of the military attache in the German Embassy in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At that time, was there a NATO mission forming in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Very close to the events of Ljuboten, NATO started a mission to collect the weapons of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And as part of your work as a reserve officer in the German army, attached, I believe you said, to the embassy there, did you work with this NATO mission?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was part of my mission there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This document has the title, "Macedonia Briefing Pack." Did you participate in the production of this document?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can I ask you, just in general terms, what was the purpose of this document? Why was it produced?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This briefing pack should inform very important persons like generals or politicians about the background of the conflict in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Was it also provided to members of the International Community?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was shared with them, but I don't know exactly if it was given to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Why were you put on this particular project to help produce this document?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So responsible for this project was, like in the first phase of this mission, Essential Harvest, to collect all available information about the Macedonian security forces as well as of the NLA, and it was primarily my mission to support with information about the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, why were you put on this project? Why you, specifically?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think why I had -- why I had a view on the NLA at this time, a very close view, and I -- they could take my notes from the past time that I had as a journalist about the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And so your knowledge was used to produce this report; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you also contribute things like contact information?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Especially phone numbers I have had were given into this briefing pack.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you produce this briefing pack all by yourself or did you work with some other people?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was working together with members of the NATO-led force. That means responsible has been a British intelligence unit, and there were also German officers and French officers who supported this project.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And so did you work closely with these other officers?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, we had regular meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: After this Macedonia Briefing Pack was produced, we see at the top here it says: "NATO Secret." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did there come a time when that classification was changed?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This classification was changed in the end of October, beginning of November, when the British left Macedonian -- Macedonia and the German took over the command. So it became clear that just for the following forces or troops, it was difficult to work with this briefing pack just if it was secret. So we opened that just for duty reasons to everybody and could so brief the new commanders and the new squadron leaders and platoon leaders and especially the liaison teams with this briefing pack as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And how about diplomats, members of the International Community?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And this time as well they were briefed with this pack.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If I could ask the Court Officer's assistance, please. I'm not going to go through every page of this document. If we could turn to what is ERN R037-6840, which is the 19th page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see a title here, "Macedonian Security Forces," and can we go to the next page, please. I see that my colleague is on his feet, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Saxon. Perhaps, Your Honour, a point of clarification. Mr. Hutsch has clearly indicated that the information which he has provided in relation to that document related to the NLA, the National Liberation Army, and it now appears that my colleague is seeking to ask him questions about the Macedonian forces. So, perhaps, if there could be some clarification on the part of the Prosecution as to whether or not Mr. Hutsch is capable of giving that evidence before he's been asked questions about the substance.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I will do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, during the production phase of this document, did you also assist by providing information and knowledge you had related to the Macedonian government and the Macedonian security forces?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But I need to know if you did. You said "we did."

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And was some of that information that you provided, did that pertain to the Macedonian Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't -- I didn't hand over detailed information about the Minister of Interior, but we were discussing exactly the schedule that you are showing me now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But did you assist in the production of this, shall I call it, organogram from the knowledge that you had and the experience that you had in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Very briefly, we see up at the top center: "Ljube Boskoski, Minister of the Interior," and then below that a serious of names and positions.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: There is a dotted line going from the name "Ljube Boskoski" to the right and then down to the words "Special Units." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then there's another line underneath the words "Special Units." On the left, we see "Red Berets, Major Goran Stojkof," and a telephone number. To the center, we see "Tigers," and the name "Goran." And then to the right, we see: "Lions, CT Unit, Goran." Can you tell us, first of all, why this dotted line appears there from the Minister to the special units?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So it was the opinion of this meeting that the Minister personally had the command over the special units.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. We see, on the left, the words, beneath "Special Units," we see "Red berets, Major Goran Stojkof." On the far right, we see "Lions," and then below that low the word "Goran." Can you tell, please, what you recall how these two apparently different units were placed there and the same first name is there?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So there were a disagreement between the officers in this meeting if the Red Berets and the Lions are the same unit or if they are different units. It was known that the Lions were headed by a man with the pre-name Goran; and that what is called here as the Red Berets, they are commanded by Major Goran Stojkof.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What did you believe?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, I believed that the Red Berets and the Lions are the same unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were the same unit?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Were the same unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: However, we see on this organogram they were listed separately. Was that the result of a disagreement?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the result of the disagreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In other words, who won that, if I can say this, if this is correct, whose viewpoint prevailed at this time?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the more British point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Based on your knowledge and experience in Macedonia during 2001, do you disagree with any other information on this diagram?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, did you also contribute information related to the Macedonian Army for this briefing pack?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn to the next page, please. It's ERN R037-6842. Did you help -- we see this diagram here. It says: "Minister of Defence and General Staff." Did you help construct this organogram?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the same way I explained like for the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, again, to the best of your knowledge, is the information on this organogram correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we can turn now, please, to R037-6857, which is about the 36th page of the Macedonian Briefing Pack. We see here a heading of a chapter: "National Liberation Army." Did you participate in the -- did you provide information in the construction of this chapter of the briefing pack?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page, please, which would be ERN R037-6858. This is an organogram entitled "NLA Military Structure." Did you help create this organogram?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see in the red box at the top, it says: "GHQ Prizren." What does that indicate?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that is the general headquarter of the NLA that was located in Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And Prizren is part of Kosovo; right?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Below that, we see a smaller red box and with the letters: "GHQ TAC," and then below that, "Sipkovica." What does that indicate?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That indicates that we had forwarded the headquarter of the NLA in the Macedonian village of Sipkovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What does "GHQ TAC" stand for?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the general headquarter tactical.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And to your knowledge, who was the head of the general headquarters?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first phase of the -- of the crisis or the conflict in Macedonia, it was General Ostreni.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you recall his first name?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: General, that means Gzim Ostreni in the rank of a general; and then I think from May on, it turned a little bit that also the political heat of the NLA, Ali Ahmeti was present in Sipkovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Below to the left, we see two smaller red boxes: "Tetovo command, Sipkovica" and then next to it, "Kumanovo command, Slupcane." What do those boxes represent?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have the two parts of the front in Macedonia, there is the western part in Tetovo. They had the command post in Sipkovica, and they were commanding one brigade. And we had another command post as responsible for the eastern part of Macedonia, Kumanovo area, that was based in Slupcane and who were leading two brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, again, when you use the pronoun "they," such as, "They had the commanding post in Sipkovica," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Below these command rectangles, we see seven smaller rectangles in red. What do these seven smaller rectangles represent?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are standing for the seven brigades of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. To your knowledge, were all of those brigades fully functioning during the entire conflict?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Just five brigades were fully functionable, and two brigades were just in training and in a build-up phase.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Which were the five brigades that were fully functioning?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were the Brigades 112th, 113th, 114th, 115th, and 116th.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So to the right we see two red rectangles with dotted lines around them. One says "117th Brigade Debar" and then the other one says "111th Brigade Debar." These were the two NLA brigades that were in formation during the crisis?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn to the next page, please. This is ERN number R067-6859.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Simply a matter of clarification. If it's the Prosecution intention to seek to tender this document, the Defence is wondering whether the Prosecution is going to ask Mr. Hutsch which part of the document he has contributed to. He's indicated, in response to my colleague's question, that he had contributed to the preparation of this particular document, but he hasn't been asked what information he was able to contribute to the preparation of that document, and that may be relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just to clarify, are we referring to the page related to the NLA that we just reviewed or to every single page in the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would, at the moment, refer to every page to which you make specific reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we can go back to the last page that we looked at, which was entitled "NLA Military Structure" at ERN R037-6858.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, Mr. Hutsch, which pieces of information on this organogram were provided by yourself?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So it's a little bit -- a little bit difficult to explain how intelligence work functions or works in this moment, because every nation is coming in with an imagination of the matter that has to be discussed. So this structure that is here was nearly complete, my introduction to this conference. And everywhere there was disagreement, it was discussed, and information by other nations flew in in creating this briefing pack. So to have here now all the detailed information, because if you say just there is a general headquarter, what brings in this information to bring us to the conclusion this is a general headquarter, there are so much information that I think we will -- we will have to continue for another -- for weeks. If you would like to have all this detailed information, we have to discuss that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Hutsch, we can do it a bit more simply. This organogram here that's entitled "NLA Military Structure," did this structure itself, the organogram itself, was this a structure suggested by you?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The information that led to this organogram were given by me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. If we could go back, please, to what is ERN R037-6841. This the organogram of the Macedonian Mini Ministry of the Interior that we saw before. Mr. Hutsch, if you can recall, what part or parts of this organogram did you contribute?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this was a suggestion by the British group in this project; and like I pointed out, we -- the German position was different, as well as the French position, to the special units, that means to the structure of the special units in this organogram. So our participation in this project was that we disagreed to this point, and this was our part in the -- in this discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And the remaining points, the remaining parts of the structure, you agreed with?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It was consistent with your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn back once more. It's actually the next page, R037-6842. It's entitled "Ministry of Defence and General Staff." We've looked at this before, Mr. Hutsch, but can you tell us what part or parts of this organogram did you contribute?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same way like I described the process before. This was also a suggestion of the British members of this group, and we discussed that, and we agreed on this -- on this special organogram.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In other words, the different military officers involved agreed on this structure, on this organogram?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn now, please, to what is ERN R037-6859. This is another organogram. It's titled "NLA Military Leadership." Did you Hutsch, did you contribute the information on part or parts of this organogram?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Which part or parts?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So as a journalist, I was the first one who said that Ali Ahmeti was the head of the NLA in Macedonia. So this information, for example, came over and flew in, in this organogram, as well as the whole of Dreni Korabu, who in my eyes was the political adviser or something like a political adviser, flew in. Yeah, and in the identification of the adviser team of Ali Ahmeti, as well as some names, came in by me. So have you to imagine also that this briefing book is the last one that we created. This was a so-called living book. That means in the first it was just a handful of information; and when I came to the German Embassy, we started to continue in writing this book, so a lot of information, for example, changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Referring to this page now, we see photographs of some people with names, silhouettes of other persons with names. Did you meet the persons that are named on this organogram?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Was that during the war?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war and during my time as an officer in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Where we see silhouettes and no photographs, why don't we see a photograph?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because there was not a photograph available in this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What do you mean by "there was no photograph available"? Why not?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of these persons didn't like to be photographed, and some of these persons hided their, I will say, face in this time and wanted to have their identity covered.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And to summarise, the information on this page, it came from you, then?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them came from me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you tell us which parts came from you?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So that Ali Ahmeti was the political leader of the NLA; the information about Dreni Korabu; I think, as well, the information about Imrez Simajili [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you agree with the other information that's on this organogram?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we can turn now to page ERN R037-6860. This is a document or an organogram entitled "NLA Military Command- GHQ." "GHQ," it stands for "General Headquarters"?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The information on this organogram, did some or all of it come from you?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What information came from you?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: For example, the nicknames of Ali Ahmeti and Gzim Ostreni; the information about Dreni Korabu; I think, also Bashram Ramadani came from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What can you tell us about the role of Gzim Ostreni, known as Plaku, during the military crisis of 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the military chief of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So what were Mr. Ostreni's responsibilities then?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was responsible for all tactical and operational leadership in the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you meet Gzim Ostreni during the crisis in 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met him during the crisis in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know what Mr. Ostreni's professional background was?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a former artillery officer in the former Yugoslavian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How about after that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then he became Chief of Staff in Operational Zone 1 of the KLA in Kosovo during the Kosovan conflict, where he was the military adviser to Ramush Haradinaj; after that, he became the Chief of Staff of the KPC, the Kosovo Protection Corps; and in the change of the year of 2000 and 2001, he became the Chief of Staff and Superior Commander of the NLA in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And at the time, 2001, when this organogram was put together, did you believe it was accurate?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn now, please, to ERN R037-6861? It's the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise once again, but so as to not create any delay or any risk that Mr. Saxon may have to go back to the documents, Mr. Hutsch has indicated that he's given some information which he contributed to the document. It may be important or it may be relevant, perhaps, to ask him where he got that information from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I will leave that entirely to you, Mr. Saxon, whether you wish to pursue that. If you don't, it's probably a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Perhaps, I can briefly pursue it. Well, I see it is a convenient time, so I will stop here, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we move back, please, to ERN R037-6858 within this briefing pack.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, we return to this organogram entitled "NLA Military Structure," and I just wanted to clarify a couple points. During the crisis time in 2001, did you visit the general headquarters of the NLA in Prizren?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't visit this headquarter directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you tell us how you received this information, that the general headquarters was in Prizren?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, there have been press discussions or briefings, press briefings, with Ali Ahmeti in this area. Second, there were information by confidential sources that told us exactly the building where this headquarter was. And the third is that in the upcoming crisis in Macedonia and in the ongoing crisis in the Cresevo valley, I got several information that this headquarter is located in Prizren for the NLA in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And for the record, are you able to provide us with the identities of these confidential sources?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Below that, we see a smaller red rectangle: "General Headquarters, Sipkovica." Did you go to this general headquarters in Sipkovica during 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you meet Mr. Ostreni or -- did you meet Mr. Ostreni there?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you have discussions with him?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At some point, did you meet Ali Ahmeti there?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see below these red boxes about the Tetovo command, Sipkovica, and the Kumanovo command, Slupcane. During the crisis time, did you go to these commands?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you have conversations with the NLA officers there?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did these conversations include information about the structure of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it had.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Down below we see the five brigades you mentioned earlier functioning during the crisis and the two brigades in Debar that were not fully operational. With respect to these five brigades, did you personally observe these different brigades?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: During 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn now, please, to R037-6859. It's the next page, please. This is the organogram entitled "NLA Political Leadership." You've told us already that you've spoken with Ali Ahmeti. Below him, we see the name "Dreni Korabu," also known as Dreni. Did you personally meet with Mr. Korabu during 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you have discussions with him about the political leadership of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And on this organogram, we see other names, but silhouettes. Can you remind us, please, did you personally meet some of the persons who are identified by name?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met everybody who is named in this organogram in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you discuss NLA activities with them?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn now to R037-6860, please. This is the organogram entitled "NLA Military Command - General Headquarters." You mentioned that you met with Ali Ahmeti and Gzim Ostreni during 2001. We see below them a line of squares. We see the name again "Dreni Korabu." Next -- to the left of "Dreni Korabu" we see the name "Nazim Beqiri." Did you meet Mr. Beqiri in 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: To the right of the name "Dreni Korabu" we see the word "logistics" and then the name Xhavit Hasani. Did you meet Mr. Hasani during 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How about the other names we see in this of squares?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was meeting as well with Bashqim [phoen] Ramadani and Basli Hajdari [phoen] and with Caesar Dimiri [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you discuss NLA operations with these gentlemen?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we can turn now to ERN R037-6861, please. This is an organogram entitled "NLA Military Command - Brigades." Did you assist in the production of this organogram?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What parts -- what parts or part of the information came from you, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I handed over a suggest in the organogram that showed how, in my point of view, the military command works, and most of these parts are in this organogram.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, which suggestions by you were incorporated into this organogram?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So that was, I will say, the middle of the organogram, that we have had seen, I think, the second, where we had the military structure of the NLA. That means Gzim Ostreni as the headquarter, the Tetovo command and the Kumanovo command, as well as the brigade commanders below.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we see a -- the bottom row, we see seven brigade commanders. So this was information provided by you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: These brigade commanders in the bottom row, did you meet these gentlemen during 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I met most of these brigade commanders. I didn't meet Zaki.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And just for the record, that is the last person reflected on the far right of the bottom row. Up above that bottom row, we see two names: Xhavit Hasani, Ibrahim Dehari. Was this information provided by you?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you disagree with this information?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't disagree, because like you see, it is not clear which function especially Xhavit Hasani had in the structure of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we can turn to the next page, please, R037-6862. It's titled -- I'll wait for it here. I'm not seeing this on the e-court. It's a document entitled "NLA Command and Control." Here it's coming, I think. Mr. Hutsch, did you assist in the production of this organogram?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This organogram is a result -- a conclusion of that what we have had seen before. So far away the information that I gave were part of this organogram.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My question was: Did you assist in the production of this organogram? Just "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. To the right of the name "Ali Ahmeti," we see a red rectangle with some question marks, and it says "Dispora Influence." It probably should say "Diaspora Influence." Can you tell us what is depicted there?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the influence that Albanians in the Diaspora, that means especially in Switzerland, in Germany, in Austria and in Italy, had on the development on the NLA in Macedonia, and especially with special taxes that had been given by Albanians in the Diaspora to pay the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: By "pay," do you mean "support"?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Why are there question marks in the silhouettes in that particular box?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the time when we -- when we created this briefing map, not already clear who is behind these people. There was just a name, Vasli Ofilio [phoen] who was clear as one member of this Diaspora influence, but it was not clear who was with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Then lower down in the middle of the picture, we see a picture "Beqiri, headquarters information press officer." Is this a person that is reflected in some of your notes from the 12th of August 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Further to the right, we see: "NLA military arm," and then further to the right, we see a photograph and the name "Fatmir." What does that indicate, this photograph with the gentleman named Fatmir?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Fatmir," that means Sokola Kuskim [phoen]. He had a special function in the General Staff, as at the end of the crisis he was responsible for evaluation and training.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did you speak with this gentleman known as Fatmir during 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And at the bottom row, we see a black horizontal line with a number of numbers, "G-1, G-2, G-3", going up to "G-8." Can you tell us what these "G" numbers indicate?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: These "G" numbers indicate the different sections that are belonging to a general staff or to a military staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you say "a military staff," are you referring to specifically the NLA, other armies? What do you mean by "a military staff"?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: These eight sections are the same in every military staff that is -- that is organised in a hierarchy.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you say "every military staff," do you mean in every army?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In every army.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when this organogram was produced, did you agree to its accuracy?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you can turn briefly, please, to R037-6868. I'm sorry, if in the English version, we could go to one page before that, please, 6868. I'm not sure if the Macedonian version we're seeing on the screen is the same. Maybe it's changing now. This organogram is titled "113th Ismet Jashari-Kumanovo Brigade." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you assist in this organogram?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I did, in the discussions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What parts of the information came from you, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I confirmed, for example, the function of Ibrahim, the function of Shpati, and the function of Jakup.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And just for the record, "Ibrahim" is the nickname underneath the photograph at the top of the organogram, "Shpati" is below that and to the left, and "Jakup" is below that and further to the left. And this information that you were able to confirm, how were you able to confirm that? Where did you get your information about this?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met these people in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: To your knowledge, is the remainder of the organogram accurate?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn, please, to R037-6870. This is an organogram entitled "114th Fadil Limani Brigade." Did you contribute some of the information on this organogram?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was my -- it was my influence that I said this command had two headquarters: One in the Kumanovo area, that means Nikustak; and the other one in Vistica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And how did you obtain that information?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was part of the normal intelligence meeting in this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No. My question is: How did you know or how did you get the information that this brigade had two different headquarters?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because this brigade was led by Gzim Ostreni in parts of the operation himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And how did you know that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because Ostreni told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can we go now to the next page, please, R037-6871. This is a continuation of the information related to the 114th Brigade. The information in this organogram, did you contribute some of it?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What parts?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That Adashi is the commander of this brigade and Kitra the Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How did you know that Adashi was the commander of this brigade?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met him in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How did you know about Kitra's role?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met him as well in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Was the 114th Brigade involved in some fighting around Aracinovo?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. She was highly involved in this -- in this fightings.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, eventually, what happened to this brigade at the end of that situation?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think as I pointed out in the very first day of my testimony, this brigade was withdrawn with support by American KFOR troops from Aracinovo to Nikustak in June, end of June, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Was the whole brigade withdrawn?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And Nikustak, is that in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And after that, did the whole brigade remain in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This remained -- just left parts of it in Macedonia, and the other part was withdrawn into Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, I would seek to tender this Macedonian Briefing Pack.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. There is a number of objections which we would raise in relation to that particular document. The first one has to do with the general reliability of this document. First, Mr. Hutsch has only been able to give evidence in relation to some but certainly not to all aspects of that document. Furthermore, in relation to certain aspects of that document in relation to which he's given information, he's refused to disclose the sources on which he says he based himself to give that information. Furthermore, there remains many grey areas as to the nature of the material that was used by him or by anyone else who contributed to that document, to prepare that document, in particular, whether they were intelligence sources, as Mr. Hutsch suggested; whether they were open sources; or whether it's any material to which we could have access. The second ground of objection, Your Honour, is a matter of relevance. We would wish to know, in particular, the date of that document and whether, depending on the answer to that question, whether this document is relevant at all to the proceedings. We have good reasons to believe that this document, and Mr. Hutsch has indicated it himself, that it was prepared after the events which are relevant to this case. Furthermore, and while I'm addressing this issue, the Prosecution has been asking questions today to this witness but also for the past two months or so about special units of the Ministry of Interior, and I believe that the time has come for the Prosecution to tell us what is the relevance of those special units to this case.
