At this stage, the Defence does not know or does not understand what the relevance of those units is. It's been indicated, at least as far as the Tigers unit is concerned, that there is no suggestion on the part of the Prosecution that they were in the village of Ljuboten during these events, so I believe that the Prosecution should now be asked to clarify this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'll try to respond briefly, Your Honour. With respect to the issue of reliability, the Prosecution believes that the objections of the Defence may go to the weight that the Chamber may decide to give to this document. However, they should not prevent its admissibility. The witness has described how this document was produced. The witness has described in detail the information on a number of the pages contained within this document. And the witness has explained how a large amount of information contained on these pages came directly from himself based on the knowledge and experience that he gained as a journalist in 2001 in Macedonia. It is true, Your Honours, that there are certain sources that -- whose information was used on certain details in this document which Mr. Hutsch will not disclose. However, again, the Prosecution submits that those sources are, at least based on the testimony that we've heard, are relatively few, because much of the material -- much of the testimony that we've heard is that a great deal of this information came from this witness's knowledge and observations during 2001. With respect to relevance, Your Honour, if I may be given a moment to ask the witness, in terms of his knowledge, as to the time period that the structures in this document refer to. May I be granted leave to do that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, the different structures, the Ministry of Interior, the Minister of Defence that we've looked at, structures of the NLA, what time period do these structures represent?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: These structures represent the time in summer 2001 to, yeah, until I left Macedonia on the 30th of November, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And by "summer 2001," can you be more specific? What months?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say roughly July, August.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: With respect, given that testimony, Your Honour, the Prosecution submits that this briefing pack, in terms of the time period, would be relevant. With respect to the issue that my colleague raised about special units, we have heard testimony, Your Honour, about the presence of certain individuals in the village of Ljuboten. We've also heard testimony about the presence of -- excuse me, about the positions of those persons within the Ministry of the Interior. And so, therefore, we believe this evidence is relevant because the evidence may show, at the end of the day, it goes to the issue of whether the accused Boskoski had effective control over the persons who were in Ljuboten on the 12th of August, 2001, whether they were involved as formal members of a so-called special unit or whether they were there in another capacity within the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Two very brief matters, first in relation to the last response given by my colleague in relation to the role of those special units. At this stage, Your Honour, we'll simply indicate that the Prosecution will be put to the task to demonstrate that this is indeed part of its case. And if, indeed, it claims that it's part of its case, we would wish an indication as to where we can locate these particular allegations which Mr. Saxon has just made. As regards the further questioning of the witness by Mr. Saxon in relation to the time, Your Honour, we -- it will be the position of the Defence that the evidence given by Mr. Hutsch in relation to this matter is, at the least, incorrect. We will be able to ask questions in relation to this matter further on in the cross-examination. At this stage, we simply wish to indicate to Your Honour that we have reasons to believe that the evidence or the answers given to the questions of Mr. Saxon are incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document will be received, Mr. Saxon. The evidence of the witness, from his personal observation alone, speaks directly to some of the contents and sufficient to justify the admission of the document. The relevance is speaking of a period of time in which this information is said to be applicable, that period including the dates that are material to the indictment. Having said those things, the Chamber makes it very clear, so that there can be no misunderstanding, that the reliability of the whole document and the weight, if any, which the Chamber will in the end be able to attach to it, are matters which will have to be considered in the light of all the evidence at a later stage. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P321, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time the Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That isn't a signal, I'm afraid, Mr. Hutsch, that you can go; it's not. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Hutsch, or good morning. My name is Guenal Mettraux, and I'm appearing together with Edina Residovic on behalf of Mr. Boskoski. You will recall, Mr. Hutsch, that you have been asked a number of questions in relation to your work as a journalist and the methods which you used in that capacity. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall having been asked general questions by my colleague about your work and method as a journalist; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you recall also giving an indication that for the past 12 years or so you worked as a freelance journalist; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all the time as a freelance journalist, especially in the period of 2001. From 1999 up to 2002, I was an employed journalist.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would I be correct, then, to understand that during the past 12 years or so, the only employment or work that you've had was as a journalist; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the parties not to overlap with questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Hutsch, I've been given the same warning as Mr. Saxon. We are being -- I am being, in any case, too fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You've indicated as well that you've taken certain steps to verify information which would be provided to you as a journalist before publishing it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And one of the ways in which you did so was to ensure that for each piece of information which you would receive, you would have two sources of information before publishing anything; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that was a way for you to guard against false or unreliable material and information; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I understand that it was your practice, when you published with the "Hamburger Adendblatt" to mention the place from which you were writing articles; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that would not necessarily be the place in relation to which you were reporting; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: My question is if you had, let's say, visited a particular place on one day and then went on to another place to write your article, the place mentioned in the article would be the place where the article was written; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where the article was written or the article was researched.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I think it was also your practice, when you wrote for the "Hamburger Adendblatt", to mention at times the city of Hamburg. Could you explain to me or to the Chamber why it was your practice to mention, let's say, Skopje and Hamburg?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was all the time then the practice when there were information from Germany that took a big part in these articles. For example, development of the German army.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So if you mention, let's say, the city of Skopje/Hamburg, that would mean you were in Skopje and received information from Hamburg in relation to that particular piece; am I --

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And a question about publication, sir, if an article is published, let's say, on the 23rd of May, 2001, let's say, at what time should you have to send the article to your newspaper for that particular issue?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That depends on the -- on the time that my chief editor gave to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what would be the latest time so that it could be published in the next-day issue?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The most latest time was 8.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And am I correct to understand, sir, that you wouldn't write an article in relation to a particular place or a particular incident unless you had, yourself, been to that place?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, you would not write such an article?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you hadn't been to such a place, you would indicate that you had received the information from a source; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You've also indicated in your evidence that it was your practice to keep careful notes about your activities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also indicated that you would do so on a daily basis generally; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to read to you a passage from your statement which you've given to the Prosecution on the 25th of August, 26th of August and 27th of August of 2005, and that's at paragraph 40, and I'll read it out slowly to you, Mr. Hutsch. You were recorded as saying the following: "Normally --"

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The witness gave a very long statement to the Prosecution years ago. Would it be possible that a copy of his statement be either provided to him or somehow could he view what's being put to him on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have the number. It's 1D234, with an ERN of 1D002567.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we have hard copies, Your Honour, if that would be easier.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Prosecutor, please. .

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, would you like to receive a paper copy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would be beautiful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If it's going to be the subject of a number of questions ...

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It may not be a bad idea, Your Honour, that he receives a copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber will have a copy, then, it appears.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps we'll distribute binders at this stage which will simplify matters a great deal, because we understand that a number of documents will be referred to, although -- with the assistance of the usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, I'll ask you to turn to page 3 of your statement. That would be paragraph 14, 1-4.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, the Court Usher will distribute to each member of the Trial Chamber two binders of documents which will relate to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry to interrupt. May I make a point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: On the 19th of June, the Prosecution received a notification from counsel for Mr. Boskoski that it was withholding documents going to the credit of this witness for cross-examination, and then the Prosecution was told the Defence will release the documents to be used with the witness before cross-examination of the witness in question. The Prosecution, at least to my knowledge, has not received any documents or a list of documents to be used during the cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand that both the list and the documents have been released.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Today, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Would it be on the way to my e-mail, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm being told by my colleague on my left that the documents have been sent to both Mr. Saxon's e-mail address and Ms. Lakshmie's as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We don't have them yet, but we will be alert to our in-boxes and hopefully we'll get them soon.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Apologies, Mr. Hutsch.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I can ask you to turn to paragraph 14 of your statement, that's page 3, and there's a sentence I would like to read out to you. It starts with the word: "Normally." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You've been recorded as saying this: "Normally, I use one notebook per day. I also do sketches and drawings of places I visit. The sketches are put normally in my notebook or on normal blank paper. I also use plastic layers which put over topographic map for marking events, locations. This technique of map drawing I learned in the German army. Normally, I do make my notes and drawings directly at the time of the events or immediately after. It is my work conduct to keep these notes archived. For the subject of this interview, I make reference to these notebooks." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you confirm that this is or this has been your practice as a journalist?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Including in the year of 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've indicated, I believe, that your language assistants or interpreters who accompanied you during your various visits would also use a similar practice of keeping notes of their visits. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And on the days when you said you visited Ljuboten on the 12th and 14th of August of 2001, did these persons keep any such notes?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You've indicated to me earlier that your sole occupation during the past 12 years was a journalist, and I think you also explained to the Prosecution that your previous occupation had been as an army captain or your last position in the army had been as an army captain in the German army. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've indicated to me that aside from a short period of time when you were unemployed, I understand, you worked most of that period as a freelancer, so it means that you were paid by the article; is that correct, that's what it means in practice, financially?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not just paid by the article. With some customers, I had a normal salary, for example, by time or by project.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps you can tell this Trial Chamber what financial arrangements you had with "Hamburger Adendblatt" in 2002?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like I told you some minutes before, I was employed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that was your only source of revenue of income during the year 2001; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And aside from the stint which you indicated from September, mid-September of 2001, to mid-November of 2001, you haven't received any money or income or other sort of gratification from any other source; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the time that you mentioned, I spent as a reserve officer in the army, and my payment was done by the "Hamburger Adendblatt" and it was given to the "Hamburg Adendblatt" by a social office of the German government.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Hutsch. And aside from the money that you received from the"Hamburger Adendblatt" and through the German army, as you've just explained, you had no other source of income; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were, for example -- there is a group that is called "VG Wort" in Germany, and that is an association of authors and of journalists who are participating in a system where everybody who is copying something in Germany has to pay for that, they give some money into this association, and this association is giving that to the authors and journalists. And I'm sure that I had, in this time as well, some money from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Any other source of revenue during 2001? Did you have any other source of revenue during 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what is "revenue during."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you receive any money from any other source during the year 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you ever work as a salesman, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: What's a salesman?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: As a retailer. Were you in the business of selling things?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you ever sell any clothes, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Clothes?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Clothing.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you sell any coffins? Those are wooden boxes to put dead people in.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I think you've indicated to the Prosecutors that you went into a number of conflict zones. Do you recall saying that? Conflict areas?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I think you've indicated that the first place in which you went was Bosnia in 1995. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you've indicated to the Prosecution that you were, "covering the conflict" at the time. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you tell which newspaper you were covering the conflict for at the time?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this time I was working for the German weekly magazine, "Die Welt."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know how many newspapers you wrote for "Die Woche" during that period?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, I understand it's the paper. I was asking you how many newspaper articles you published during your time in Bosnia, approximately, Mr. Hutsch.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately, 20. As well, in this time for the books, too, the "Tagesblatt."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then you went on to another conflict zone; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this was the time of my training as a journalist, because I was trained as a journalist in 1995 and up to 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And where did you receive that training, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I told you, in the "Buchsuda Abendblatt" and then "Die Woche."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And where were you based during those two years?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was based in Germany in Hamburg and in Buchsuda.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Am I correct to understand that the next conflict zone, so to say, where you went was Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's incorrect, because I did a trip to Chechnya in 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did you work for a particular newspaper during that period?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you cover the Chechen conflict for anyone?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I just had a small stop there for two weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what sort of occupation were you involved in during those two weeks in Chechnya?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was to find out what was going on in Chechnya and to see if it was a place where I could work.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then what was the next conflict zone where you went after Chechnya, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next conflict zone was Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the Defence counsel and the witness to pause between questions and answers and try to avoid overlapping. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We've been warned again, Mr. Hutsch. You indicated that you then went to Kosovo, and I understand that in your testimony in the Milosevic trial you've indicated that you published many and regular articles about that conflict. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you tell what newspaper or media outlet you published for?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've -- I was working for the German magazine "Der Stern" as well as in the early case of this -- in the early phase of this conflict, for the daily newspaper "Die Woche."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall how many articles you would have written for both "Der Stern" and "Die Woche"?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Der Stern," I think it was all in all five, and "Die Woche," ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also indicated in your evidence in the Milosevic case that during your time in Kosovo, you met a large number of the leaders of the KLA, is that correct, including Mr. Ahmeti and Mr. Ostreni?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also met Mr. Ahmeti and Mr. Ostreni during your time in Macedonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall how many times you met Mr. Ostreni, in particular?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: All in all?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ninety, up to 100 times.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in all those contacts, they related to your work as a journalist, sir?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So which part of those 90 to 100 contacts related to your work as a journalist?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fifteen.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What about the rest?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rest was my mission during I've been in the German Embassy.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So between 15 September to 15 November 2001, you met Mr. Ostreni between 75 and 85 times; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's incorrect. Between the 21st of September and the 30th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for the correction. So during that period of approximately two months, you met Mr. Ostreni between 75 and 85 times; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You also met, I understand, Mr. Veliu; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you met him during your time in Macedonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you had a good relationship with Mr. Veliu; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Veliu, Fasi, was the uncle of Mr. Ahmeti; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he is the uncle, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you remember meeting Mr. Veliu on the 30th of September of 2001 in a restaurant?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think I met him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall meeting him again three days later?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, you just indicated to me that I was incorrect in suggesting that you had a good relationship with him. I'd like to put that to you. Is it correct that he would refer to you as "Ambassador Hutsch"?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, definitely not, because I was not an ambassador.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I understand you were not an ambassador, but I'm putting to you, sir, that he was referring to you as "Ambassador Hutsch." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He never was calling me so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you told me that you did not have -- when I asked you whether you had a good relationship with him, I'm going to ask you this: Did you make any promise to Mr. Veliu to assist him with personal matters?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Did you promise to Mr. Veliu to assist with his son or his brother?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was one thing, but I don't know if it's connected with Mr. Veliu. There was, in the end of November, a discussion with another man about probably a nephew of Mr. Veliu with the last name Osmani.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you there, sir. The question I'm asking you is about the end of September and relates to the brother of Mr. Veliu. Can you recall an incident between yourself and the brother of Mr. Veliu?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness what is under tab 4 of the binder, and the document is 1D-281 with an ERN of 1D-002812.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You will have the document appearing on your screen, Mr. Hutsch, on your right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It's tab 4, Your Honour, in the binder, in the first binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So as you can see, Mr. Hutsch, this is the book of memoirs from Mr. Fasi Veliu. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look on the left side of this document, there's an excerpt, the translation of one particular page of the book of Mr. Veliu and, the date which it refers to is the 30th of September 2001 in Tetovo. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In fact, can I ask you to direct your attention to the "ii" saying: "The German ambassador's wish ..." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what he wrote.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to read to you what he wrote. It says this: "The German ambassador [Realtime transcript read in error "chancellor"], Franz Hutsch, and a companion was in the restaurant first room. He expressed a wish to meet us. 'I want to shake your hand,' he said. We invited him to our table. He came with his friend. We drank together. We spoke of the amnesty. I explained the reason for my imprisonment in Constance." Then there's a quote, "'We have one aim,'" and the quote says, "'For new generations to survive and advance,' I said, but they are abducting our young people and the place they are held is unknown. They ill treat them." "'Do you have documented cases?'" "'Yes,' I said. 'My brother abducted six weeks tomorrow.' "We made a human gesture. We released all the prisoners of war. We promised cooperation. We wish you success. I saw them off and said good-bye in friendly fashion." Does that refresh your memory, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It refreshes my memory as to what Mr. Veliu was pointing out there, because it was the phase in the operation Essential Harvest where we had to find out how both sides are willing to -- yeah, to live in harmony together in the future. And like I pointed out some minutes before when the Prosecutor asked me, the influence of Mr. Veliu was quite high especially on Ali Ahmeti.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you there. I'm not asking you to tell us, at this stage, what the role of Mr. Veliu is. Do you recall this particular incident now?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall that we spoke about -- we spoke about the amnesty, and we spoke about how he would like to hand over some documents for people who are still in Macedonian prisons.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall also that he asked you to assist with him brother, don't you?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know what he would like to have with his brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can we turn to the next page of that document, please. That's 1D00-2813.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Just a correction, Your Honour. At page 66, line 16, Mr. Hutsch is referred as "the German chancellor, Franz Hutsch." It would be "the German ambassador," the chancellor being the Prime Minister in Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, can you see that second page of the document?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Veliu says the following: "I phoned the German ambassador, Franz Hutsch, asked about my brother, Hoxhdi [phoen]. 'I know where he is. He's in prison in Skopje,' he said. I'm trying to visit him. I thanked him and promised the work meeting with Ali. I told Gzim, my nephew, Falija [phoen], my sister, Nazmi [phoen]." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that conversation with Mr. Veliu at the time?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, there was a phone call. I think the most easiest way to bring clearance to all these things is that we start from the 22nd of September up to the 30th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you there, Mr. Hutsch. For the time being, we're going to stay on this document. We're going to go one step at a time and see a lot of incidents and events together. Can you recall this conversation with Mr. Veliu ?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall promising assistance in relation to his imprisoned brother?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can recall that I promised to find out what was going on with all in contact with the conflict, arrested Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall a particular promise made to Mr. Veliu in relation to his brother or not?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not had particular in relation to his brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the work meeting which you promised with Alija, am I correct to understand that it was Ali Ahmeti he was referring to?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it also correct, Mr. Hutsch, that as part of your work in Kosovo during the Kosovo conflict, you were, in fact, embedded with the KLA?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you reported, in effect, by their side. You attended, if I may use that term, several conflict zones and operations together with the members of the KLA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: As part of your work as a journalist, Mr. Hutsch, you broke quite a few big stories; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what is a big story, but I did a lot of stories, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, there's a few of those stories which I would like to go through with you, and the first one you mentioned during your testimony in the Milosevic case, where you appeared as a Defence witness. You remember, I'm sure, mentioning the fact that you said you had an interview with Ratko Mladic. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this interview which you said you had with Mr. Mladic took place after the indictment of Mr. Mladic by this Tribunal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware when this Tribunal already opened that Mr. Mladic was indicted. I don't know at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to assist you with that in a minute. But you would agree that this was quite a big story, a big event in your journalistic career, to interview Mr. Mladic?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was not a big story, especially not in that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, do you know of any other journalist who, since the indictment of Mr. Mladic, has claimed to have an interview with him?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, first, I would like that you would provide me with the date when the indictment took place, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I would ask you to answer the question, sir. I'm going to give you all the documents you need in a minute. But could you tell me, do you know of any other journalist who claimed to have interviewed Mr. Mladic since 1996?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before -- before 1996, there were a lot of journalists, and so my interview was nothing special in this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What about after 1996, sir? Do you know of any journalists who claim to have interviewed Mr. Mladic?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you tell this Chamber how you managed to interview Mr. Mladic in 1996?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I did the interview in 1995, in December 1995. It was published, as far as I remember, in January 1996, but it was just normal because Mr. Mladic was available in Bosnia and the Republic of Srpska at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And so can you tell me how you managed to get in touch with Mr. Mladic?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got in touch over the interpreter that I worked with and over my Serbian sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you tell us who this interpreter is who put you in touch with Mr. Mladic?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you tell us who is that Serbian source you've just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, that during the Milosevic trial you were asked to state the newspaper in which you say you published this story; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that the Prosecution pointed out that they had been unable to trace that particular document; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you able today to state what newspaper you have published this story in?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of them, and that's what I said in this time, was the "Neue Osnabrucker Zeitung".

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct. You were asked several times, and you said that you believed that you published it in the"Neue Osnabrucker Zeitung". Is that your evidence today, sir?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown what is tab 8 of the Court binder, and it is 1D323 with an ERN of 1D003015. This is under tab 7, I apologise, of the binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, what will appear to you on your computer screen is a letter written by the Defence of Mr. Boskoski, directed to the"Neue Osnabrucker Zeitung", the newspaper which you just mentioned as being the place where you say you have published this piece.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I draw your attention to the second paragraph of that document, starting with the words "As part." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It says: "As part of its investigation, the Defence received information that Mr. Frans-Josef Hutsch might have published some articles in your newspapers. The Defence hereby kindly asks you to inform us whether the above-mentioned information is true or not." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: "Moreover, if the above-mentioned report is true, the Defence hereby kindly ask you to provide us with the information in what capacity did Mr. Hutsch publish those articles. Finally, the Defence wishes to know whether Mr. Hutsch published any article in the newspaper during June September 2001 period." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And on the next page there is the signature of counsel. I'll now ask the registry to show what is under tab 6 of the Court binder with an ERN 1D324 and with -- it's a number, I apologise, Exhibit Number 1D324 with an ERN of 1D 003017. Sir, that is the response that we received from the"Neue Osnabrucker Zeitung", and it says: "Dear Ms. Residovic, concerning your letter from 26 March 2007, we found that Frans-Josef Hutsch didn't publish any article in the year 2001 in our newspaper. As freelancer, Mr. Hutsch published the following two articles in our newspaper in 2003 and 2004." And then it refers to the two pieces which you've published in the newspaper. Sir, is that correct that you never published that Mladic story in the"Neue Osnabrucker Zeitung"?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, and I think that should be part of the second letter from the "Neue Osnabrucker Zeitung" that was sent to you, that I was not really sure that I was giving this interview to this "Neue Osnabrucker Zeitung", and in the time that you are asking, I was employed in the "Hamburger Adendblatt" so there would be no chance for me to give them any article.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that your evidence, sir, now, that you published in another newspaper other than the "Osnabruker Zeitung"; are you telling me that you now recall that you published it somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you tell me where you published it, sir?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to find out that in my archive.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But, sir, you were asked the very same questions in the Milosevic case, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, and as far as I know in the Milosevic case, this matter was already disclosed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to come to that, sir. But this is what Mr. Nice said in the Milosevic trial. This is the transcript at page 32997. For Your Honours' assistance, this is under tab 5 of your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE SAID THIS
utterances.text: "I can just tell the Court and thus inform the witness that we made every effort through the newspapers he identified yesterday," "He" being you: "The to get a published version of the article and interview, but were unsuccessful, and I think we even got the newspaper concerned to search its archives, but we couldn't find it." Do you recall Mr. Nice making that comment?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I can assist you a bit more, sir. If the Registry can bring up 1D284 with an ERN 1D00-2820. That's the English version. And for your assistance, Mr. Hutsch, there is a German version at 1D2818. Do you recognise this document as the one -- Your Honour, it's under tab 8 of the binder. Do you recognise this document as the one you produced in the Milosevic proceedings, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will agree, I hope, that there's no marking, no sign, no indication of any newspaper of any sort on this piece of paper?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was all -- that was that what I found in the hurry of time, this time, in my -- in my archive, and that was faxed to the Tribunal in this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But, sir, that was two and a half years ago, is that correct, the Milosevic proceedings?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you were also asked by the Defence, through the Prosecution, to provide information in relation to that particular document, do you remember, sometime this year, earlier this year?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got the information from the -- from the Prosecution not to provide that, it was just a question if I could provide, and after my knowledge, and that should be part of my statement and my testimony in the Milosevic case, that already this case was closed, and I can't see the relation between the Milosevic case in the moment and this case in the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me deal with the issue of relevance, perhaps. My question was: Were you asked by the Prosecution, on behalf of the Defence, to provide information as to the newspaper in which you claim you published that story? Were you asked by the Prosecution that question? Were you asked to provide that information?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was asked to provide this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall what you told the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told the Prosecution that in this statement and my testimony, this part has been disclosed, so it was -- it was finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I don't understand your answer, sir. Perhaps it's my fault. But what exactly are you saying you told the Prosecution when you were asked to provide that information? Can you clarify this?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So Mr. Kay --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm asking you about Mr. Saxon, Mr. Hutsch. What did Mr. Saxon ask you to provide him? What was your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreters ask you again to please pause between questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues...] -- from the defence, and there were -- not Mr. Saxon, it was Mr. Kuehnel who did this during a telephone call, and I told him that already this Milosevic case or this Mladic interview was already finished in this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we'll come back to that question in a minute, sir. But do you recall that you were asked already during the Milosevic proceedings to provide clear information about your publications, and in particular in relation to that article? Do you recall being asked that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I were asked to that, yes, I was asked that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll just read to you the paragraph or the passage to you fair to you, Mr. Hutsch. It's in the Milosevic transcript at page 33023, and it's again in tab 5 of the Court binders, Your Honour. This is an exchange between you and Mr. Kay, counsel for Slobodan Milosevic at the end of the trial, at the end of your evidence. Mr. Kay said this: "And I appreciate you will have to go into your records, but it may be helpful to the Court if you were able to produce a schedule of where this article was published and the dates. Is that possible for you to do that?" And that's what you answered: "Well, all the articles that I have written and that have been published, it's an agreement between the client and the author that these publications are also returned in manuscript form, and it's stated where it appeared or a copy of the newspaper, or the newspaper itself. I've collected all of them, and all of the articles I've written and have been published have been duly archived." Then Mr. Kay said: "If you could, over the period of the next week, say, if you have an opportunity, would you be able to provide a table listing where and when this was reported?" Do you recall Mr. Kay asking you that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And your answer, sir, was: "Yes, of course." Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you remember providing a list of your publications to Mr. Kay, as you had undertaken to do?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we have to ask Mr. Kay, because I was together with my lawyer and I think I gave a list to my lawyer. But what I think is there is some things in -- has been lost in the translation in the very beginning of your quote.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, there's nothing that was recorded that has been lost, Mr. Hutsch, I can assure you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm very sorry for the interruption, and I don't know if, after the Chamber hears the Prosecution's comment, whether the Chamber will wish the witness to leave the courtroom for a while, but the Prosecution, at least, is confused as to the relevance of this line of questioning related to this witness's testimony two and a half years ago in the Milosevic trial, to the evidence that he has given in this case. And I'm wondering whether my colleague could at least clarify what the relevance is; and if my colleague prefers, perhaps the witness could be excused while he does that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I think it would be proper that the witness be excused for a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will take a minute?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It might take two, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're getting near the next break time. It might be fairer to Mr. Hutsch for him to go, knowing he's got at least 35 minutes of break in which to relax.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Hutsch, would you be good enough now to treat this as the break, and it will be some time, depending on how long this one or two minutes lasts, it will be sometime a little before 1.00, I expect, that we resume.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, would you like me to address Mr. Saxon's question at this stage?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the position of the Defence -- and perhaps we should go into private session at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm afraid when we adjourned I overlooked the fact that we were still in private session. So we continue now. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall a moment ago I asked you a question about your interview with Mr. Mladic, and my question was as follows: "And can you tell this Chamber how you managed to interview Mr. Mladic in 1996?" Do you recall my question?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And your answer was: "I did the interview in 1995, in December 1995." Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'd like, with the Court's assistance, again the Milosevic transcript of your testimony at page 33011. This is tab 5, and it has an ERN 1D00-3218. And then, sir, in this page that you have in front of you, you can see you're being asked a number of questions about this particular interview, and then if I may delay your attention at line 19, you say this: "That was 1996, I did the interview in 1996, and I would have used it then." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So that's not 1995, that's 1996. So which version are you adopting now, sir?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in 1995. I have to check that, if it becomes so important.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you recall, sir, that in any case, that it was after Mr. Mladic had been indicted by the Tribunal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know. Meanwhile, Mr. Mladic was indicted in 23rd of July in '95, and he was -- he wasn't any more in charge of the Chief of Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska in March 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, the question is: Can you recall now whether the interview took place after Mr. Mladic had been indicted? Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. He was indicted in July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that this alleged interview with Mr. Mladic took place after this indictment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we can turn to tab 8 of the binder. That's 1D284, 1D 00-2820, that's the English, and the German, Mr. Hutsch, is 1D00-2818. So here there's a list of questions and Mladic, so I suppose the questions were asked by you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And Mr. Mladic is General Mladic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And was anyone else present during that meeting between you and Mr. Mladic?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an interpreter present.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Anyone else?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were some advisers of Mr. Mladic present as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall the names of those people?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We haven't been introduced.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So they were just sitting around?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall where this meeting took place, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to go into the interview that you recorded there, and it says -- there's a question, and it starts with: "General, what is life like as an alleged war criminal who many would like to see before the Tribunal in The Hague and rather today than tomorrow?" So that's your opening question to Mr. Mladic?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And he says: "Why war criminal? Do you know more than I do?"

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So, sir, did you know at the time that he had been an indicted war criminal by the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know if I really was aware if -- that he was indicted as a war criminal. The purpose of this question was that was clear that after the -- the incidents in Srebrenica, Mr. Mladic -- it was known that he was involved in these war criminals, and that was the reason why I was asking the question in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the answer of Mr. Mladic suggests that he wasn't aware that he was being a war criminal, or at least regarded by one. He asked you, "Do you know more than I do?" Does that suggest that he didn't know he was an indicted war criminal?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he's arguing in the same way like both accused are arguing, that he's doing a defence line, that he said, "I'm not a war criminal at all; and if that is so, do you know more than me, because I am innocent."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, when you refer to both accused, do you refer to Mr. Tarculovski and Mr. Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And your suggestion is that they are doing a defence line; is that your evidence, sir?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this interview with Mladic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No, no. I'm not talking about Mr. Mladic, sir. You said both accused are arguing that he's doing a defence line. When you refer to both accused, are you referring to Mr. Tarculovski and Mr. Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you suggesting they are doing a defence line?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that they are accused war criminals who are indicted here.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what did you mean when you made a reference to both accused here?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That the answer, if I would have done an interview in the same opening, I think I would have got the same answer from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer, Mr. Hutsch. Then you go on to ask Mr. Mladic that: "For instance, because of more than 7.000 dead Muslim in Srebrenica ..." And Mr. Mladic is recorded as saying: "A number I'm absolutely not familiar with." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then you record yourself as putting that question to

utterances.speaker: MR. MLADIC
utterances.text: "Another part is that the men were separated from women, union protection forces watched as men were executed." And then you recorded Mr. Mladic as saying: "That's nothing but a cock-and-bull story." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then further down this document, you say -- you record yourself as putting a question for Mr. Mladic: "For such complex issues like the attack on protected area, the support of President Milosevic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters would appreciate it if Mr. Mettraux will slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: He will attempt his best.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You said this: "For search complex issues, like the attack on protected areas, the support of President Milosevic is certainly helpful." And then you recorded an answer by Mladic: "Let me put it differently. I don't take any orders from Milosevic. We are grownup enough to solve our problems ourselves." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then the interview ended when Mr. Mladic is recorded as saying: "It amuses me that you don't believe me, that you don't believe we can take care of ourselves; but, at the same time, you think we massacred 7.000 Muslims. How does that fit together? That's a contradiction in terms." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's what you say you obtained from Mr. Mladic --

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- some time in 1995 or 1996; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to go back to the Milosevic -- your Milosevic testimony. You remember that I asked you a number of questions about requests that were made to you by the Prosecution on behalf of the Defence to obtain information pertaining to that article; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you said: "And it was not Mr. Saxon; it was Mr. Kuehnel during this telephone call. And I told him that already this Milosevic case or this Mladic interview was already finished in this time." Do you recall telling me that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that what you recall Mr. Kuehnel to tell you at that time?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Kuehnel was calling me in this moment, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's what you communicated to Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall if Mr. Kuehnel responded to that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: He just took the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like the witness to be shown 1D-243. It's ERN 1D00-2669.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is this in the binders?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm trying to locate the document in the binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps 89.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would like to refer to a slightly different document. I'm sorry, Your Honour. This is tab 9 of the document. We're going to go to 89 in a minute, Your Honour. I apologise. I apologise to you, Mr. Hutsch, as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is Rule 65 ter 236, with 1D00-2655. It's 1D-236. I apologise to the Registry, 1D-236, with 1D00-2655, and it's tab 9, Your Honour, of the binder? We seem to have a problem with the document on the screen. It should be 1D-236, 1D-2655. Thank you. That is the right document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Hutsch, for the delay. This, again, is a letter from the Defence of Mr. Boskoski, this time to the Office of the Prosecutor. As you can see, it's dated 30 March 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I can ask the Registry to go directly to page 4 of that document, it's 1D00-2658.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can I ask you to focus on paragraph 24, Mr. Hutsch, if you can. And if the -- yes. Thank you. On the 30th of March, we ask the following of the Prosecution: "In the transcript of his evidence in the Milosevic case, dated 12 October 2004, Mr. Hutsch says that he published an interview which he had with General Ratko Mladic in 1996, transcript 32964. "The Defence would like to receive a copy of that article or information allowing the Defence to locate it; title of the article, date of publication, name of newspaper. "The Defence hereby notes that the plain text of the interview you disclosed as Rule 68 material, apart from not constituting Rule 68 material, is not sufficient for the purpose of the Defence investigation."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then if I can ask that the Registry turn to what is 1D-238, with an ERN number 1D00-2661.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, that's a letter from the Prosecution, the OTP, written by or signed by Mr. Saxon, and it's addressed to Ms. Residovic. And it's in response to two letters of the Defence of 14 of April, 2007; and then if you look at the first paragraph, it also responds to our letter of the 30th of March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is it in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Tab 10, Your Honour, I apologise, tab 10 of the binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask you again to focus on number 24, the same number as previously, in this letter. It says: "Mr. Hutsch suggests that you speak with Attorney Stephen Kaye for more information." So that's the response you gave to the Prosecution in response to our request to obtain more information pertaining to this particular article, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps, Your Honour, if I can move into private session for a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then there's a second point, Mr. Hutsch, which you can see in the letter. It says this: "During the Milosevic proceedings, Mr. Hutsch undertook to provide you with a list of his publications as a journalist. The Defence would be most grateful to receive such a list from you, if one has indeed been provided to you, or with an indication to the effect that none has been provided to you." And then there's other matters. If I may ask the Registry to go back to the first page of that document and focus on the first section of that document this time. Are you able to read the text, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is the response from Mr. Kaye, and it's dated 25th April 2007: "Subject, Prosecutor versus Boskoski." It says: "Dear Mr. Mettraux, in response to your e-mail letter, one, I did see an article produced by Mr. Hutsch of an interview with or statements made by General Mladic which were recorded by him." I do not have that document now. Could I tell you -- or where to find it, although I have a recollection that at the end of his testimony I returned all papers, not exhibits, to Mr. Hutsch. That would be my normal practice. I cannot recall whether it would be a newspaper or magazine or on the internet, so I cannot define the source. At the time, this was not of importance to me, but the fact of his conversation with Mladic was important. The length of the piece was not long, one, one and a half pages or columns. I do not have a list of journals in which Mr. Hutsch published articles. I was concerned with whether he had seen or heard rather than anything he might have written." Is it correct, sir, that you never gave this list, a list of publications, to Mr. Kaye as you had undertaken?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct also that you never provided him with any information about the whereabouts of this alleged interview with Mr. Mladic?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not after I went -- I left here and even not in the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So is the situation this, sir, that no one, not even yourself, are able to say where a world-exclusive interview with Mr. Mladic was published?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's first not a world-exclusive interview with Mr. Mladic, and, second, it was not an important one. So it was an interview, and in the moment I'm not able to provide you with any further information.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So let's start first with your first comment. It's not a world-exclusive interview. Can you now recall anyone, any journalist, claiming to have interviewed Mr. Mladic after his indictment or in 1996?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't research in this in the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, there's another story which I would like to now review with you which also relates to your testimony in the Milosevic case. Can you recall writing or contributing, rather, to a piece about the alleged involvement of the German Secret Services into organising riots in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will agree, I hope, that this was a big story.

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a good story, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this was a story that you stand by to this day, sir; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But it's a story that was criticised very heavily in some newspapers in Germany; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In one newspaper.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, would you agree that it may have been more than one?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was criticised in one.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We're going to come back to that. But is that correct that the newspaper which you are thinking about right now made a pretty serious attack not only on the quality of your reporting but on your honesty and integrity as a journalist?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't do that. I didn't see a serious attack against that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that your evidence, sir, that you didn't feel a personal attack from this newspaper; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I felt attacked by this newspaper, but for that you have to see the background.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, my question is, sir: Did that newspaper suggest in not so many words that you had fabricated part of your story?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't that what the newspaper suggested?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the newspaper which you have in mind, is it the "Frankfurter Allgemaine Zeitung"?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would agree, I hope, that it's, perhaps, one of the most reputable or, perhaps, even the most reputable newspaper in Germany?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would also agree, I hope, that you were criticised, among other things - if "criticised" is the right word - for your famous use of what they said, "sources"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's something the author did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the line of his story was essentially to say that you claim to have had access to information that no one else ever had; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's one of the part he wrote, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I would like to show you that article, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It's at tab 11 of Your Honours' binder. It's 1D-280 with an ERN of 1D00-2802.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Mr. Hutsch, there is a German version of it at 1D00-2799. Just as a general question, Mr. Hutsch: Do you agree that this newspaper essentially touched upon two categories of activities of yours; one was these reports about riots in Kosovo, and the other one was your testimony in the Milosevic case. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, you are quite.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So if you look at the document there, you can see it comes from the archives of the ""Frankfurter Allgemaine Zeitung"," and the date of the page is 3rd of June 2005. Do you see that? It's at the top of either of the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the date --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: 3rd of May, I apologise. Thank you to Mr. Saxon. I apologise, Mr. Hutsch. It is not relevant, the date, but I apologise for thinking that the 5th was June or July.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you see the dates in the top right corner in German?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And there's a title in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would like to indicate to the Trial Chamber that at this stage this is only an unofficial translation, the documents haven't been -- well, we're awaiting the official translation from CLSS.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There's a title, sir, of the piece, which is somewhat clumsily interpreted that: "In doubt for the defendant Milosevic, the truth about the Racak massacre, why a dubious report of the ZDF Horta [phoen] Journal ^^^ Anchorage, the Serbian appealers." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then I would ask you to go immediately to the second full paragraph of this article, which was written, am I correct, by Mr. Matthias Rub; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Matthias Rub, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And Mr. Rub is a journalist with the FAZ, "Frankfurter Allgemaine Zeitung"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So if you turn to the second paragraph, which starts with the words, in English in any case, "Two authors of the Horta Journal." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANS-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It says: "Two authors of the Horta Journal, the editor, Hans Ulrich Gak [phoen], and the free journalist, Frans-Josef Hutsch, in the broadcast reports on the 18th and 20th of November, 2004, claimed nothing less but to have found the wire-puller of the riot's programmes."
